title: Irreducible characters of finite nilpotent and elementary groups are monomial
statement:
A finite group $N$ is nilpotent if there is a finite central series $1=N_0\leq N_1\leq\cdots\leq N_c=N$ of normal subgroups with $[N,N_{j+1}]\subseteq N_j$, where $[N,N_{j+1}]$ is generated by commutators $xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ with $x\in N$ and $y\in N_{j+1}$. Let $N$ be such a group and let $W$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional irreducible complex representation, meaning that it has no nonzero proper invariant subspace. There are a subgroup $K\leq N$ and a homomorphism $\lambda:K\to\mathbf C^\times$ such that
$$W\simeq\operatorname{Ind}_K^N\mathbf C_\lambda$$
as complex $N$-representations. Here $\mathbf C_\lambda$ is the line with $k\cdot z=\lambda(k)z$, and the induced representation is the quotient of $\mathbf C[N]\otimes_{\mathbf C}\mathbf C_\lambda$ by $[nk]\otimes z=[n]\otimes\lambda(k)z$, with action by left translation on $[n]$. The field $\mathbf C$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. In particular the same conclusion holds for every elementary group $E\simeq C\times P$, where $C$ is cyclic of order prime to a prime $p$ and $|P|=p^a$ for some $a\geq0$.

proof.text: Prove the nilpotent-group assertion simultaneously for all finite nilpotent groups by strong induction on $d=\dim_{\mathbf C}W$. The case $d=0$ is excluded by $W\ne0$. If $d=1$, choose $0\ne w\in W$ and define $\lambda(n)$ by $\rho(n)w=\lambda(n)w$. Invertibility and the action law give $\lambda:N\to\mathbf C^\times$. With $K=N$, the maps $[n]\otimes z\mapsto z\rho(n)w$ and $zw\mapsto[1]\otimes z$ are inverse equivariant maps for the stated induction quotient. This proves the base case.

proof.text: For $d>1$, not every $\rho(n)$ is scalar: otherwise every line would be invariant, contradicting irreducibility. In the given central series choose the smallest $j$ such that some $x\in N_j$ acts nonscalarly. Every element of $H=N_{j-1}$ then acts by a scalar. Put $A=H\langle x\rangle=\{hx^m:h\in H,m\in\mathbf Z\}$. Since $H$ is normal, this is a subgroup. For $n\in N$, the central-series condition gives $nxn^{-1}=[n,x]x\in Hx$ and $nHn^{-1}=H$; hence $nAn^{-1}=A$. The operators of $A$ are scalar multiples of powers of $\rho(x)$, so they commute, and its image contains the nonscalar operator $\rho(x)$. This uses only the central-series definition and the action law; no faithfulness or abelianness of $A$ is asserted.

proof.text: The complex field is algebraically closed by lem-weil-complex-algebraically-closed and has characteristic zero. Apply lem-per-normal-commuting-weight-induction to $G=N$, this normal subgroup $A$, and $W$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 2 and the original irreducibility assumption. Obtain $W=\bigoplus_{\chi\in X}W_\chi$ and, for a chosen $\chi\in X$, an irreducible representation $U=W_\chi$ of $T=T_\chi$ with $W\simeq\operatorname{Ind}_T^N U$. There must be at least two weights: a single weight would give $W=W_\chi$, making every operator of $A$ scalar, contrary to Step 2. Since every summand is nonzero, $0<\dim U<d$.

proof.text: The group $T$ is finite and nilpotent: intersect each term of the original series with $T$. The resulting normal subgroups of $T$ start at $1$ and end at $T$, and $[T,T\cap N_{i+1}]\subseteq T\cap[N,N_{i+1}]\subseteq T\cap N_i$. Apply the strong induction hypothesis from Step 1 to the nonzero irreducible $T$-representation $U$, whose dimension is strictly less than $d$ by Step 3. This gives $K\leq T$ and $\lambda:K\to\mathbf C^\times$ with $U\simeq\operatorname{Ind}_K^T\mathbf C_\lambda$.

proof.text:
Inducing the isomorphism from Step 4 sends a generator $[n]\otimes u$ to $[n]\otimes f(u)$; equivariance of $f$ makes this well-defined and the inverse is obtained from $f^{-1}$. Now use the transitivity isomorphism of lem-per-finite-group-induction-calculus, for the finite groups $K\leq T\leq N$ over $\mathbf C$, which is algebraically closed of characteristic zero. Together with Step 3 this gives
$$W\simeq\operatorname{Ind}_T^N U\simeq\operatorname{Ind}_T^N(\operatorname{Ind}_K^T\mathbf C_\lambda)\simeq\operatorname{Ind}_K^N\mathbf C_\lambda.$$
The induction-calculus node uses precisely the quotient and left action in the item, so this proves the representation-level assertion and completes the induction.

proof.text: For $E\simeq C\times P$, use lem-per-finite-prime-power-central-series to choose a central series $1=P_0\leq\cdots\leq P_c=P$. The sequence $1\leq C\times1\leq C\times P_1\leq\cdots\leq C\times P_c=C\times P$ is a normal central series: $C$ is cyclic, hence abelian and central in the product, and $[(c,p),(c',q)]=(1,[p,q])$. If $c=0$, this is just $1\leq C$. Pull the sequence back along the stated group isomorphism to obtain such a series for $E$, and apply the nilpotent-group assertion just proved. This includes $a=0$, $P=1$, and $C=1$; the prime-to-$p$ condition on $|C|$ is allowed but unnecessary for this consequence.
